title: Maneul Jangajji Soy-Pickled Garlic
shortDescription: Peeled garlic is submerged in a boiled, fully cooled soy-vinegar brine and held only under refrigeration for a short, unvalidated pickling window.
culturalContext: Maneul jangajji is Korean pickled garlic, with whole-bulb and peeled-clove methods, staged brines, aging periods, and regional preferences. This conservative draft is refrigerator-only and not a canning or fermentation process.
author: {{LEGAL_NAME}}

totalTime.display: 7 days plus about 1 hour preparation and cooling

equipment: Clean glass refrigerator container with nonreactive lid

instructions.heading: Inspect and clean
instructions.action: Discard moldy, bruised, soft, sprouted, or damaged garlic; wash hands and use a clean container and tools.
instructions.safetyNote: Do not use recalled, temperature-abused, or spoiled peeled garlic.

instructions.heading: Make brine
instructions.action: Combine soy sauce, commercial 5%-acidity vinegar, water, and sugar; bring to a full boil while stirring.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Sugar dissolves and brine reaches a full boil.
instructions.safetyNote: Hot acidic brine can burn; avoid splashing and use nonreactive cookware.

instructions.heading: Cool completely
instructions.action: Cover the brine against contamination and cool completely, then refrigerate until cold.
instructions.safetyNote: Do not pour warm brine over garlic for an extended room-temperature hold.

instructions.heading: Submerge cold
instructions.action: Place garlic in the clean refrigerator container, pour over cold brine, apply a clean nonreactive weight, cover, label, and refrigerate immediately.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Cloves are fully submerged and the container is labeled.
instructions.safetyNote: This is not canned, shelf-stable, or fermented; never store at room temperature.

instructions.heading: Pickle under refrigeration
instructions.action: Keep continuously at or below 40°F / 4°C for 7 days, checking that cloves remain submerged and discarding the batch for mold, gas, bulging, slime, or off odor.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Cloves remain submerged with no spoilage signs.
instructions.safetyNote: Do not taste a suspect batch; when in doubt, discard it.

instructions.heading: Serve with clean utensils
instructions.action: Remove only the needed cloves with clean tongs and return the container immediately to refrigeration.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Master container remains cold and uncontaminated.
instructions.safetyNote: Use within 7 days after the first serving pending process review; never reuse the brine.

grillSetup: Not applicable; this banchan is prepared without a grill.
targetInternalTemperature: Bring the brine to a full boil, cool it completely, then keep the garlic continuously at or below 40°F / 4°C; this is not a shelf-stable process.
visualDonenessCues: Brine shows no mold, gas, bulging, slime, or off odor
foodSafetyNotes: Use commercial vinegar labeled 5% acidity and do not change the vinegar-water ratio.
This is a refrigerator pickle only—not canned, fermented, or shelf-stable.
Keep continuously at or below 40°F / 4°C with garlic submerged.
Discard the entire batch for mold, gas, bulging, slime, off odor, temperature abuse, or uncertainty.

allergens.crossContactWarning: Contains soy and wheat/gluten; verify soy sauce and vinegar labels.

substitutions: Do not alter the vinegar, water, garlic, or container process without a tested recipe and qualified process review.
ingredientSourcing: Choose firm sound garlic and commercial vinegar clearly labeled 5% acidity.
makeAhead: The required 7-day refrigerated pickling period is part of the draft and still needs qualified process validation.
storage: Keep continuously at or below 40°F / 4°C. Use within 7 days after first serving and within 14 days of assembly pending qualified review; discard sooner for any concern.
reheating: Do not reheat or can this draft.
leftovers: Never reuse brine or return served cloves to the master container.
servingSuggestions: Serve a small refrigerated portion beside grilled foods.

faq.question: Is this shelf-stable?
faq.answer: No. It must remain refrigerated and is not a canning or fermentation recipe.

faq.question: Can I reduce the vinegar?
faq.answer: No. Do not change the acid-water ratio without a tested process.
